No specific religious freedom legislation or extreme statements found in Smith's record on this topic. Her overall record reflects balance between protecting religious practice and maintaining anti-discrimination protections for LGBTQ individuals. She supports full LGBTQ equality but has not staked out extreme positions on religious exemptions in either direction.

Smith voted YEA on the Respect for Marriage Act (Senate vote 362) codifying same-sex marriage federally. She signed a letter urging reversal of visa denials for same-sex partners of LGBTQ diplomats and is a consistent LGBTQ+ rights advocate, reflecting support for full federal recognition and benefits for same-sex marriages.

OTI explicitly records Smith as opposing school vouchers as creating two-tiered systems and she advocates for free all-day kindergarten and expanded federal financial aid for public schools. She consistently opposes diverting taxpayer money to private institutions through voucher programs.

OTI records Smith's position as no privatization nor cuts to benefits (August 2019) and she backs raising the payroll tax cap instead of raising the eligibility age to fund Social Security. She opposes transitioning Social Security to private accounts, reflecting a stance of protecting and modestly strengthening the current program.

Smith supports fair trade policies that help Minnesota workers and introduced the Trade Cheating Restitution Act (2025) targeting Chinese dumping practices harming honey producers. OTI records her concern about steel dumping and support for cracking down on nations violating trade rules. She backs USMCA and is neither a free-trade absolutist nor a blanket-tariff protectionist.

Smith advocates for a fairer tax code that supports working families not just the wealthiest Americans. OTI records her as supporting reversing federal income tax cuts for the wealthy and backing inheritance taxes. She supports modestly increasing taxes on high earners while maintaining current rates for working and middle-class families.

Smith voted NAY on S.9 (Senate vote 100, March 2025), which would have required transgender athletes to compete based solely on biological sex assigned at birth for Title IX compliance. Her NAY vote reflects support for transgender athletes competing on teams matching their gender identity after completing basic transition documentation.

Smith voted YEA on Reed Amendment 299 (Senate vote 76, February 2025) to ensure continued U.S. support for Ukraine against Russian aggression, though the amendment was rejected 47-53. She has consistently supported Ukraine's defense and signed letters asserting the value of foreign assistance commitments.
